trust_decision.summary: On read-back of a persisted state machine, Kryo decides which Java classes may be instantiated from the stored bytes. At the pinned commit none of the three Kryo factories that serve persisted contexts ever calls setRegistrationRequired, so class identity inside the stream is trusted and any class on the classpath (including gadget-chain classes) can be named by the payload; the decision point is therefore 'which classes may Kryo resolve' inside each factory, before the first read.

landing_point.why: It is the only place that configures a Kryo instance for the state machine context in the module named after Kryo ('Kryo-based persistence backends'), and it is where the three default serializers are installed, so anybody reading the advisory summary lands here and adds setRegistrationRequired(true) in configureKryoInstance.

fix_sites.entry_point: new KryoStateMachineSerialisationDefaults.registerDefaults(Kryo), called from all three factories
ZookeeperStateMachineEnsemble(CuratorFramework, String) start-up read of current state
sample bean definitions for JPA/MongoDB/Redis runtime persisters

O3_reason_to_dismiss: ZooKeeper is a cluster/ensemble feature in a top-level module that is not one of the Spring Data 'persistence backends' (JPA/Mongo/Redis) the report and samples point at, and ZookeeperStateMachinePersist does its own hand-rolled ThreadLocal<Kryo>, so a fix to KryoStateMachineSerialisationService never reaches it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Reading back what was already written must keep working. The bytes on the wire are produced by AbstractPersistingStateMachineInterceptor.buildStateMachineContext, which puts a fresh DefaultExtendedState (an ObservableMap wrapping a ConcurrentHashMap, with a non-static inner listener) plus message headers (MessageHeaders with UUID id and Long timestamp) and the application's own S/E enums into the context; so a bare setRegistrationRequired(true) makes every existing deployment fail on both write and read, and pre-registering a fixed list additionally renumbers Kryo registration ids so contexts persisted by the previous version no longer decode - the serializer is documented as a byte-compatibility contract.

O6_input_shapes: the outer persisted StateMachineContext blob itself vs. each nested value
each of the eight class-resolving slots the serializer reads: event, state, eventHeaders, extended-state variables, child contexts list, history-states map, id, child-references list
a registered container (HashMap/ObservableMap/ArrayList) carrying unregistered values inside it, e.g. arbitrary objects as extended-state variables or header values
application S/E enums: unregistered types that must be rejected, and the same types supplied through the new Consumer<Kryo> hook so they are accepted
null slots (state or event absent) mixed with the remaining slots
three storage shapes for the same bytes: a repository entity byte[] column (JPA/MongoDB/Redis entity), a raw Redis value keyed by machine id, and ZooKeeper node data (current state and log entries)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a leader-election ensemble that builds (or exposes) its own ZookeeperStateMachinePersist / its own Kryo factory
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it already duplicates both super-constructors and the published fix added the kryoCustomizer overload only to the parent, so this wrapper still has no way to register application enums - a maintainer would plausibly add its own persist next.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second StateMachineContextRepository for another key/value store that copies this hand-rolled ThreadLocal<Kryo>
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this exact pattern already exists once and diverged from the kryo module, so any new key-value backend author would copy it rather than route through KryoStateMachineSerialisationService.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third read path (snapshot vs. log replay) with its own Kryo instance or its own registration policy
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the class already has two detached read entry points (read and readLog) and log replay is invoked separately from ZookeeperStateMachineEnsemble.java:444, so splitting their serialisation config is a natural-looking change.

O10_build.toolchain: Gradle 8.14.5 via wrapper, Spring Boot 3.5.15 plugin, Kryo 4.0.3, multi-module (12 modules + samples)
O10_build.project_tests: spring-statemachine-kryo has KryoStateMachineSerialisationServiceTests.java:36-53 (plain JUnit5/AssertJ round-trip, runs with no service) and StateMachineContextSerializerTests.java:40-42, which documents the serializer byte layout as a compatibility contract. No security/negative test exists at the pinned commit; the fix's KryoStateMachineSerialisationDefaultsTests is a new file, absent from the pinned tree. Zookeeper tests use curator-test's embedded TestingServer; JPA uses HSQLDB; Redis and Mongo tests need real servers (no flapdoodle or testcontainers in the build).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add kryo.setRegistrationRequired(true) inside KryoStateMachineSerialisationService.configureKryoInstance - one file, one line - which covers only the JPA/MongoDB/Redis-entity path, leaves the hand-rolled Redis context repository and ZooKeeper persist open, and breaks every existing user because their S/E enums and headers can no longer round-trip and there is no registration hook.

out_of_scope_notes: A separate non-Kryo read path exists in the same repository: spring-statemachine-data/src/main/java/org/springframework/statemachine/data/support/StateMachineJackson2ResourceReader.java:95,117 deserialises JSON model resources; it is developer-supplied model data rather than a persisted state-machine context, so it is outside this advisory's property and was not pursued.

The same commit also changes the Redis key format (bare machine id -> 'ssm:context:' + id) in RedisStateMachineContextRepository.save/getContext; that is a separate hardening concern from the class allowlist and is only recorded here as a compatibility observation.
